qualification: The published lineage end to end with every release's own published bundle, images and launcher on one Linux arm64 Docker engine: a fresh v0.4.6 installation (published 0001-0010, pgvector 0.8.6), upgraded to v0.4.7 with only the commands both bundles ship (published 0011-0012), then to v0.4.8 with the v0.4.8 upgrade command (0013-0018). Logical backup on the same host. Not off-host recovery, not Kubernetes, not a production-sized dataset.

outcome.v046_to_v047_published_commands: passed: published 0001-0012, every data table and the 337-event audit prefix unchanged, v0.4.7 verify passed; v0.4.6 writers served again for about 4 s between the backup and stop, as UPGRADING.md warns
outcome.first_v048_upgrade: passed: clean, on the legacy 0.8.6 vector catalogue, 244 s end to end, 119 of 121 tables unchanged before verify
outcome.incompatible_releases: passed: v0.4.7 gateway, read-only check and migrator refused 0018 without writing
outcome.interrupted_stamp: passed: refused for serving by both gateways; the v0.4.8 migrator repaired only the stamp
outcome.pgvector_catalogue_update: passed: ALTER EXTENSION vector UPDATE TO '0.8.7' with writers stopped, a no-op migrate, restart and v0.4.8 verify
outcome.rollback_by_restore: passed: the v0.4.7 bundle restored before-0-4-8 and opened tenant key version 1 with 398 audit events; the logical restore recreated the vector catalogue at 0.8.7
outcome.second_v048_upgrade_with_injections: passed: lock bound and writer drain each refused without loss, then the same command resumed to complete

host.drill_engine: docker:29-dind (docker@sha256:08a98015fce594af7c382883bea080ea206de74402a95da9dc52b6428c8cd121), Docker 29.9.3 linux/arm64, Compose v5.7.0, containerd snapshotter, cgroup v2, 16816517120 bytes of memory, in one privileged container with its own /var/lib/docker volume
host.runner: inside the drill container: Alpine 3.24.4 with bash, curl, util-linux, coreutils, postgresql17-client, python3 and jq; the launchers ran as uid 1000 in the engine socket's group; the home directory's setgid bit was cleared before the first preparation
host.isolation: The launchers fix the Compose project at synveda-evaluation, and this host's engine already holds volumes under that name, so the drill used its own engine, which started with no images, containers or volumes.

digest_method: snapshot.py: one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction as the bundled superuser synveda_owner over the local socket; per public table, row count and SHA-256 over the sorted row_to_json text of its columns, with the column set frozen from the comparison's starting snapshot; ledger entries matched by version; audit prefix digest over seq, prev_hash, hash, occurred_at, actor, action, resource, outcome, payload and trace_id up to a bound.
drill_notes: The first v0.4.8 upgrade's script then waited on the lock helper indefinitely. When the helper was stopped, the script ran on for about 30 seconds (one v0.4.7 read-only check, the two reruns and one v0.4.8 verify) before it was stopped too. Those steps are recorded above.
The drill's ledger comparison first sorted entries as text, which misaligns 0010-0012 with 0002-0009; entries are matched by version instead.
